question: Why did two runs halt with 'the reset to <sha> before the retry failed'?

telemetry.reason: the reset to 397dcba before the retry failed
the worker returned no STATUS report

transcript.event: the worker's hand-back arrives as an <agent-message> prompt (its report was the word 'pending')
UserPromptSubmit (H1 handBack) prints: the run stopped at T03 ... Reason: the reset to 397dcba before the retry failed
Stop hook system message: T03 on sonnet-medium failed, retrying a tier up (the state SubagentStop wrote last)
git status --short is empty and HEAD is 397dcba: the other hook's reset had succeeded
Stop hook blocks and asks for the sonnet-high retry: the saved state is the retry, not the halt

cases.seen: H1 reported a halt while H4's retry state won; the user was told the run stopped although it had not.

telemetry.reason: the reset to a5c9605 before the retry failed

attempts.transcript: UserPromptSubmit (H1) at 01:50:40.051Z prints 'Reset to a5c9605; retrying one tier up', and the retry is dispatched

telemetry.reason: the reset to a5c9605 before the retry failed

attempts.transcript: UserPromptSubmit (H1) at 01:50:58.702Z prints 'Reset to a5c9605; retrying one tier up', and attempt 3 is dispatched

cases.seen: here H1 won and the run went on; the halt line came from the SubagentStop (H4) settle that lost.

cause: For a background worker, the hand-back prompt (H1 handBack, UserPromptSubmit) and SubagentStop (H4 stop) fire within about 50-100 ms of each other. Each reads the state while the attempt is still in flight, so both settle it, and on a retry both run `git reset --hard` in the same repository at once. The second meets the first's .git/index.lock and fails. Git's stderr was discarded, so the halt reason did not say this; the pairs of telemetry lines 50-80 ms apart, the clean tree at the expected HEAD afterwards, and the reproduction below show it.

ruledOut.windowsFileLockByWorkerProcess: not seen: the tree was clean at the recorded HEAD right after the halt (lexical case), so nothing blocked the clean
ruledOut.ignoredOrReadOnlyFiles: git clean -fd leaves ignored files alone, and the other hook's identical reset and clean succeeded

reproduction.how: a temporary repository with 300 tracked files; per trial, all files modified and an untracked file added, then two node processes run the old resetTo (git reset --hard -q <base>, then git clean -fdq) at the same moment

sample.stderr: fatal: Unable to create '<repo>/.git/index.lock': File exists.

new.note: the same race with the new resetTo, which repeats a command failing with a lock-type error after waits of 100, 200, 400, 800 and 1500 ms

fix: lib/git.js resetTo repeats a command that fails with a lock-type error (a Git .lock file, or a Windows sharing or permission error) a bounded number of times, and on failure returns the git command and the first line of its stderr, which lib/settle.js puts in the halt reason. The double settle itself (H1 and H4 both judging one attempt) is not changed here.
